people.name: Nehemiah, son of Hacaliah
people.role: King’s cup bearer who becomes governor of Judah
people.relations: He is the son of Hacaliah and brother of Hanani. He serves Artaxerxes. Sanballat and Tobiah oppose him.
people.meaning: Nehemiah weeps when he hears Jerusalem’s wall is broken. He asks the king to send him, and the wall is finished in fifty-two days. He makes the nobles give back fields taken for debt. Later he returns and throws Tobiah’s goods out of the temple. He shuts the gates on the Sabbath.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hanani, Nehemiah’s brother
people.role: Brother who brings the news about Jerusalem
people.relations: Nehemiah calls him his brother. He shares charge of Jerusalem with Hananiah.
people.meaning: Hanani comes to Susa with men from Judah. They say the wall is broken and the gates are burned. Nehemiah weeps, fasts, and prays. After the wall is built, Nehemiah puts Hanani in charge of Jerusalem.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Moses
people.role: Earlier leader whose law the people read
people.relations: The book calls him God’s servant. Ezra reads from the book of his law.
people.meaning: Moses does not act in this book. Nehemiah’s prayer repeats God’s word to him about scattering and gathering. Ezra reads his law to the people. They swear to walk in it.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Artaxerxes, the Persian king
people.role: Persian king who sends Nehemiah
people.relations: Nehemiah is his cup bearer. The queen sits by him in chapter 2.
people.meaning: He sees that Nehemiah is sad and asks why. He agrees to send him to Judah. He gives letters and sends army captains and horsemen. In the king’s thirty-second year Nehemiah goes back to him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Asaph, keeper of the king’s forest
people.role: Keeper of the king’s forest
people.relations: He keeps the forest for Artaxerxes. Nehemiah asks the king for a letter to him.
people.meaning: Nehemiah 2:8 is his only verse. The letter asks him for timber. The timber is for the gates, the city wall, and Nehemiah’s house. Asaph himself does not speak.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Sanballat the Horonite
people.role: Enemy who mocks and threatens the wall builders
people.relations: He works with Tobiah and Geshem. A grandson of Eliashib the high priest is his son-in-law.
people.meaning: He is grieved when Nehemiah comes. He mocks the builders before the army of Samaria and plans an attack. He asks Nehemiah five times to meet him. Nehemiah will not come. In chapter 13 Nehemiah chases away his son-in-law.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Tobiah the Ammonite
people.role: Enemy with friends and family ties in Judah
people.relations: He is the son-in-law of Shecaniah. His son Jehohanan marries the daughter of Meshullam.
people.meaning: He says a fox could break the builders’ wall. He and Sanballat hire Shemaiah to scare Nehemiah. Nobles of Judah write to him, and he sends letters to frighten Nehemiah. Eliashib later gives him a temple room. Nehemiah throws his goods out.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Geshem the Arabian
people.role: Enemy who asks Nehemiah to a meeting
people.relations: He acts with Sanballat and Tobiah. Sanballat’s letter calls him Gashmu.
people.meaning: He joins Sanballat and Tobiah in mocking the builders. He and Sanballat ask Nehemiah to meet in the plain of Ono. Nehemiah says they mean to harm him and will not go. Sanballat’s letter says Gashmu reports that the Jews plan to rebel.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Eliashib, the high priest
people.role: High priest who builds the sheep gate
people.relations: He is the father of Joiada. A son of Joiada is son-in-law to Sanballat.
people.meaning: Eliashib and his brother priests build the sheep gate and set up its doors. In chapter 13, Eliashib the priest makes a large temple room for Tobiah. Nehemiah calls this evil and empties the room. Nehemiah also chases away Eliashib’s grandson.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The wall builders
people.role: Families, priests, and workers who repair the wall
people.relations: They include priests, goldsmiths, rulers, and men from Jericho, Gibeon, and Mizpah.
people.meaning: Each group repairs its own part, and many work across from their own houses. The nobles of Tekoa will not help. When enemies plan an attack, half hold spears while half work. Each builder wears his sword.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shallum and his daughters
people.role: Ruler and his daughters who repair the wall
people.relations: Shallum is the son of Hallohesh. He rules half the district of Jerusalem.
people.meaning: Nehemiah 3:12 is their only verse. Shallum and his daughters repair a part of the wall. They are the only women the repair list names as workers.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Meremoth, son of Uriah
people.role: Man who repairs two parts of the wall
people.relations: He is the son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz.
people.meaning: He repairs a part of the wall near the fish gate. Later in the list he repairs a second part. It runs from the door of Eliashib’s house to the end of the house.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Meshullam, son of Berechiah
people.role: Builder whose daughter marries Tobiah’s son
people.relations: He is the son of Berechiah. His daughter is the wife of Jehohanan, Tobiah’s son.
people.meaning: He repairs two parts of the wall. One is across from his own room. Chapter 6 says his daughter married Tobiah’s son. That tie is one reason many in Judah were sworn to Tobiah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Nehemiah, son of Azbuk
people.role: District ruler who repairs part of the wall
people.relations: He is the son of Azbuk. He rules half the district of Beth Zur.
people.meaning: Nehemiah 3:16 is his only verse. He repairs the wall across from the tombs of David and on to a pool. He is not Nehemiah the son of Hacaliah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: David
people.role: Earlier king named in places and in worship
people.relations: The book calls him the man of God. Solomon is his son.
people.meaning: David does not act in this book. Builders repair the wall near his tombs and his city’s stairs. The Levites praise as he commanded. The singers carry his musical instruments at the wall.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Families burdened by debt
people.role: Parents and children short of food and land
people.relations: They cry out against their brothers the Jews. The nobles and rulers are their lenders.
people.meaning: The people and their wives cry out. They have pledged fields, vineyards, and houses to buy grain and pay the king’s tribute. Some sons and daughters are now servants. Nehemiah is angry, and the nobles swear to give everything back.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shemaiah, son of Delaiah
people.role: Man who tells Nehemiah to hide in the temple
people.relations: He is the son of Delaiah. Nehemiah says Tobiah and Sanballat hired him.
people.meaning: Nehemiah visits his house. Shemaiah says men are coming to kill Nehemiah. He tells him to shut himself inside the temple. Nehemiah will not go in. He sees that God did not send Shemaiah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Noadiah, the prophetess
people.role: Prophetess Nehemiah names in a prayer
people.relations: Nehemiah names her after Tobiah and Sanballat. He adds “the rest of the prophets.”
people.meaning: Nehemiah 6:14 is her only verse. Nehemiah asks God to remember her among those who tried to frighten him. The book gives none of her words.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hananiah, commander of the fortress
people.role: Governor of the fortress put over Jerusalem
people.relations: Our reading text calls him the governor of the fortress. He shares charge of Jerusalem with Hanani.
people.meaning: After the doors are set up, Nehemiah puts him in charge of Jerusalem with Hanani. Nehemiah calls him faithful and says he feared God above many. The two must keep the gates shut until the sun is hot.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zerubbabel
people.role: Earlier leader named in the return lists
people.relations: He is the son of Shealtiel. The lists name him with Jeshua.
people.meaning: Zerubbabel does not act in this book. His name stands first in the old list Nehemiah finds. Chapter 12 lists the priests and Levites who came up with him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jeshua, son of Jozadak
people.role: Earlier priest named in the return lists
people.relations: He is the son of Jozadak and the father of Joiakim. Eliashib is his grandson.
people.meaning: Jeshua does not act in this book. The old list names him right after Zerubbabel. Chapter 12 lists the chief priests of his days. It then follows his family down to Jaddua.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Nebuchadnezzar
people.role: King of Babylon named in the return list
people.relations: He is king of Babylon. The list says he carried the people away.
people.meaning: Nehemiah 7:6 is his only verse. He does not act in this book. The list counts the people who came back from where he carried them.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The returning families and temple workers
people.role: Families and temple workers in the earlier return list
people.relations: They came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua. Nehemiah finds their list.
people.meaning: Jerusalem is large, but few people live in it. Nehemiah plans to count the people and finds this older list. It counts 42,360 people by family and town. Some priests could not find their records and were kept from serving.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Asaph, the singer
people.role: Earlier singer whose sons sing at the temple
people.relations: Mattaniah, Uzzi, and Zechariah are named among his sons.
people.meaning: Asaph does not act in this book. The return list counts 148 singers from his family. His sons lead the thanksgiving and blow trumpets at the wall. Chapter 12 looks back to the days of David and Asaph.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ezra
people.role: Priest and scribe who reads God’s law
people.relations: The people ask him to bring the book. Nehemiah the governor and the Levites stand with him.
people.meaning: Ezra stands on a wooden pulpit and reads the law from early morning until midday. The people weep, and he and the leaders tell them not to mourn. The next day they study the law and keep the feast of booths. At the wall, Ezra the scribe walks before one company.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The teachers of God’s law
people.role: Levites who help the people understand the reading
people.relations: Chapter 8 names thirteen of them, with Jeshua first. They work beside Ezra and Nehemiah.
people.meaning: They read the law clearly and give the sense. The people understand and weep. The Levites calm them and say the day is holy. In chapter 9, Levites stand on the stairs and lead the long prayer.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Sherebiah
people.role: Levite who explains the law and leads the prayer
people.relations: He is listed among the Levites with Jeshua, Bani, and Kadmiel.
people.meaning: He is one of the Levites who help the people understand Ezra’s reading. In chapter 9 he stands on the stairs and cries out to the LORD. He helps call the people to stand and bless God. His name is on the sealed covenant.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shabbethai, the Levite in Nehemiah
people.role: Levite who teaches and has charge of outside work
people.relations: Chapter 8 lists him among the teaching Levites. Chapter 11 names him with Jozabad.
people.meaning: In chapter 8 a Levite named Shabbethai helps the people understand the law. In chapter 11 Shabbethai and Jozabad are chiefs of the Levites. They have charge of the outside business of God’s house.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Joshua
people.role: Earlier leader named at the feast of booths
people.relations: The book calls him the son of Nun.
people.meaning: Nehemiah 8:17 is his only verse. The people build shelters and live in them for the feast. The verse says Israel had not done so since his days.
people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abraham
people.role: Father of the people, named in the prayer
people.relations: The prayer says God chose Abram and named him Abraham.
people.meaning: Abraham does not act in this book. The prayer says God brought him out of Ur of the Chaldees. God found his heart faithful and promised the land to his offspring. The prayer says God kept that word.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Sihon
people.role: Earlier king whose land Israel took
people.relations: The prayer names him with Og king of Bashan.
people.meaning: Nehemiah 9:22 is his only verse. The prayer says God gave Israel kingdoms and peoples. Israel took the land of Sihon, the land of the king of Heshbon.
people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Og
people.role: Earlier king of Bashan whose land Israel took
people.relations: The prayer names him right after Sihon.
people.meaning: Nehemiah 9:22 is his only verse. The prayer says God gave Israel kingdoms and peoples. Israel took the land of Og king of Bashan.
people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The families making the covenant
people.role: Men, women, and children who swear to keep God’s law
people.relations: They join their brothers the nobles, who sealed the written covenant.
people.meaning: They take an oath to walk in God’s law. They promise not to marry their children to the peoples of the land. They will not buy on the Sabbath. They will bring wood, first fruits, and tithes to God’s house.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jeshua, son of Azaniah
people.role: Levite who seals the covenant
people.relations: He is the son of Azaniah. He is not the priest Jeshua, the son of Jozadak.
people.meaning: Nehemiah 10:9 names him first among the Levites who sealed the covenant. The verse says nothing more about him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Aaron
people.role: Earlier priest whose sons serve at the temple
people.relations: The priests are called his sons or descendants.
people.meaning: Aaron does not act in this book. The covenant says a priest of his line must be present when Levites take tithes. In chapter 12 the Levites set apart a share for his sons.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Levi
people.role: Father of the Levites, named in the covenant
people.relations: The Levites are called his children.
people.meaning: Levi does not act in this book. The covenant says the children of Levi will bring grain, new wine, and oil. They bring them to the temple rooms.
people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The families settling in Jerusalem
people.role: Households chosen or willing to live in Jerusalem
people.relations: They come from Judah and Benjamin, with priests, Levites, and gatekeepers.
people.meaning: The princes already live in Jerusalem. The rest cast lots, and one family in ten moves into the city. The people bless the men who offer to go. The city had been large with few people in it.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Solomon
people.role: Earlier king named in worship rules and a warning
people.relations: He is David’s son and king of Israel.
people.meaning: Solomon does not act in this book. The singers and gatekeepers serve as David and Solomon commanded. In chapter 13 Nehemiah says foreign women caused even Solomon to sin. He uses this to warn men who married foreign women.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The singers at the wall’s dedication
people.role: Two companies who give thanks on the wall
people.relations: Ezra the scribe goes before one company. Nehemiah follows the other.
people.meaning: The singers gather from the villages around Jerusalem. Nehemiah sets two companies on the wall, and they walk in opposite directions. They meet and stand in God’s house. The joy of Jerusalem is heard far away.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Balaam
people.role: Earlier man hired to curse Israel
people.relations: The Ammonites and Moabites hired him against Israel.
people.meaning: Nehemiah 13:2 is his only verse. The people read that he was hired to curse Israel. God turned the curse into a blessing. After hearing this, they separate the mixed crowd from Israel.
people.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: The foreign wives and their children in Nehemiah
people.role: Wives and children from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab
people.relations: They are the wives and children of Jews. None of them is named.
people.meaning: Nehemiah sees Jews who married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab. Half their children cannot speak the Jews’ language. He curses the men, strikes some, and makes them swear. The book gives none of the wives’ or children’s words.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

contextGuide.title: Nehemiah: context and evidence
contextGuide.description: Explore the book’s larger concerns through selected passages and relevant evidence.

steps.title: A wall requires permission and resources
steps.text: Between the king’s question and his own answer Nehemiah prays (verse 4). Then he names a time, letters for safe travel, and timber (verses 6–8). A bulla of the Persian period shows how letters were sealed. Verse 8 lists three uses for the wood. Safe travel and building materials depend on the king’s support. Nehemiah credits “the good hand of my God.” He also inspects the walls himself before he speaks to anyone (verses 12–16).

steps.title: A shared building project does not remove inequality
steps.text: The enemy in this chapter is inside the walls. Verse 1 notes that wives join the outcry. Their argument in verse 5 is shared family: the same flesh, the same children. Yet their daughters are already in bondage, and the fields belong to others. Deuteronomy 23:19–20 forbids charging interest to a fellow Israelite. In verse 10 Nehemiah admits that he and his men have also lent. He ends the practice and gives up his own allowance (verses 14–18).

steps.title: Public reading requires understanding
steps.text: The people themselves ask for the book (verse 1). Verse 2 names the audience as men, women, and all who could understand. Verse 7 names thirteen Levites who helped them. Verse 8 gives their method: read clearly and give the sense. The goal is that the people understand what is read. Verse 12 traces the day’s joy to that understanding. On the next day they act on what they find (verses 14–16).
